why: Correctness and tests are required because this PR adds a new rewrite to RexSimplify. A reviewer needs to check that it is safe under three-valued logic, handles non-determinism, works with the notTerms/unknownAs interplay, and that the edit-while-iterating loop is sound, and the tests must cover those cases. Performance is required because RexSimplify is a hot path and the new pairwise scan is quadratic, capped at 20 terms.

Correctness, tests and spec_conformance are required because the PR is a large feature: it changes the parser grammar to accept OFFSET expressions without parentheses, adds CEIL-based OFFSET+FETCH pushdown in the Sort/Union rules, and changes how dialects write OFFSET back to SQL, with the SQL standard and other databases as reference points. Backward_compat, error_model, user_docs and user_value are required because the PR renames public CalciteResource message methods, changes the minimum row-count estimate for non-literal OFFSET, changes error messages and adds a new user-facing feature that needs reference docs.

Correctness is required because this bug fix changes when an optimizer rule may fire, and the reviewer must check that the empty-group-set guard covers every case, including the other join side and grouping sets. Tests are required for a bug fix and must be checked for whether they fail without the fix and whether the metadata-dependent positive case is sound.

correctness is 2 because the new isValid check has branching logic: a MAP field-count rule and a single-column fallback that re-derives the type from the column. It also reports the wrong derived type when validation fails. tests is 2 because this is a new behavior, and the test does not cover MULTISET, a MAP with two fields of the wrong type, or the exact failure message.

Correctness is labeled 2 because the fix now maps both sides through getFunctionKind(). A call bound to POSITION could then match any candidate that also maps to OTHER_FUNCTION, such as a user function with the same name, so the filter may become too loose or ambiguous. Tests is labeled 2 because this is a bug fix: the test covers only the duplicated standard table and does not check what happens when a different OTHER_FUNCTION operator is also a candidate.

The PR changes how string literals are quoted in generated Pig Latin, so it needs a security (injection) check and a spec_conformance check against Pig's escape rules for backslash, quotes and other escapes like \n and \u. The bug fix needs a correctness check of the escape order and of the null/'null' path, and a tests check that the regression tests can actually fail.

This PR adds a new join algorithm, so correctness (NULLs, collations, operator normalization), tests and user_value need a focused check, and performance needs one because it claims a faster algorithm but gives no benchmark. The rule is also on by default in the standard rule sets and in Programs, which changes existing plans (CombineRelOptRulesTest.xml changed), so backward_compat and surprising_behavior need focused review too.

Correctness is labeled 2 because this bug fix changes when the validator pushes an outer ORDER BY into the inner query, so the edge cases need checking: an inner OFFSET with no FETCH, both present at once, and when the query gets wrapped. Tests are labeled 2 because a bug fix owes regression tests, and the new test covers only FETCH, not OFFSET, the case with both, or a no-rewrite case.

Tests (label 2) is required because this is a validator bug fix, so regression coverage is owed. Correctness (label 2) needs a focused pass because the fix is non-trivial: it changes common-column expansion for ORDER BY, adds alias-precedence handling in nthSelectItem, and loosens GROUP BY matching in AggChecker with stripAs, and any of these could match the wrong expression.

tests, performance and contradictions are required because the re-enabled plan test locks in a plan with a cross join (EnumerableNestedLoopJoin condition=[true]) plus a semi-join, which looks like a regression. The description calls this plan "more optimized" and says the filter literal is folded, but the filter still has CAST($t4):INTEGER = 1997.

Correctness is required because the validator bug fix expands USING/NATURAL common columns and strips AS inside the rollup check, which raises edge cases such as aliased, nested and qualified columns. Tests are required because this is a bug fix, and the new cases only check .ok() and could miss related failure paths.

Security, correctness and spec_conformance are required because the PR changes how string literals and identifiers are escaped in nine dialects and five adapters, and each backend has its own lexing rules. The Netezza and Hive-regex outputs, and the unknown-dialect default that now doubles backslashes and so changes data on standard backends, need checking. Backward_compat, surprising_behavior, user_docs and change_description are required because the default changes silently and the new system property needs docs. Tests are required because the Cassandra test only checks the driver, not CassandraTable. Error_model is required because the new Geode/Elasticsearch identifier checks add new error paths.

build_ci is required because the PR rewires javac through a Gradle toolchain, adds the foojay plugin, switches to --release 8, and changes every CI job, including the ErrorProne and Checker Framework overrides and the removed java.version cache inputs. user_docs is required because the JDK needed to build Calcite changes to 25, and the developer build docs (howto) likely don't say so yet or explain the jdkBuildVersion property and auto-download.

Correctness and backward_compat are required: the public 3-arg constructor's limit is now relative, so an explicit Long.MAX_VALUE overflows in `limit + absolutePosition`, and the new lazy init adds a round-trip. Tests (no coverage for that case or the pre-9.3 path), performance (the speed-up has no measurement), error_model and surprising_behavior (mark() now logs at SEVERE and swallows the error, skip() counts bytes past the end) and change_description (a user-visible fix with no changelog entry) are required too.

correctness: some java-format messages contain a single apostrophe (e.g. "senza un'operazione" in the CommandComplete ''{0}'' message), which MessageFormat reads as the start of a quote, so the placeholder and the rest of the message are lost; all translated strings with placeholders need checking. contradictions: the rewritten .po header disagrees with itself and with the PR (PO-Revision-Date and Last-Translator still say 2018 while the changelog is dated 2026, and "Claude" is named as a copyright holder), even though the description says only empty entries were filled.

user_docs and correctness are required because the PR changes the public docs site, and each of the 436 slug-to-page mappings needs checking: that it points to the page that actually holds the content (for example ext, arrays, replication, or java8-date-time) and that no legacy slug is missing.

build_ci and security are required because the PR changes the CI workflows, the Codecov setup and the Gradle report config, and it commits a Codecov upload token in plain text while the secret handling changes for fork PRs. contradictions is required because the new build.gradle.kts comment says the XML report is used by omni.yml, but the upload now happens in main.yml.

tests is 2 because this bug fix comes with no regression test for close() with unflushed BlobOutputStream data, and change_description is 2 because a user-visible fix owes a changelog entry. concurrency is 2 because moving closed=true after the flush changes the close/cleanup lifecycle: if flush throws, the object stays open and the fastpath close is skipped.

Correctness, tests and backward_compat are required: the PR changes when the prepared-statement cache is invalidated (the epoch bump from ParameterStatus, the scan that is skipped once the server reports search_path, and baseline handling) and changes observable behavior on PG 18+, so the new version-dependent test needs checking. Change_description is required because this user-visible change comes with no changelog entry.

change_description is required because this PR is the release changelog, so every entry, PR link, date, and category (Fixed vs Changed vs Added) has to be checked. contradictions is required because CHANGELOG.md, the 42.7.13 docs page, and the backfilled 42.7.12 page must agree with each other and with the merged PRs. For example, the 42.7.13 summary says reWriteBatchedInserts is now "capped" at the protocol limit, but the entry describes the cap being raised from 128 to 32768.

Security, correctness and tests are required: this is a fix for a channel-binding downgrade advisory, and neither test exercises the new post-negotiation isPlus check. Error_model, backward_compat and change_description are also required: the change adds two new connection-rejected errors, connections that used to succeed under require (Ed25519 certificates) now fail, and there is no changelog entry for a security fix.

The description says a shared checkNotEmpty guard was added to six methods and that one rejectsEmptyInput test covers every entry point, but the diff only adds an inline check in toTimestamp and two toTimestamp tests, so contradictions, change_description (also no changelog entry), correctness (toDate, toLocalDate, toLocalDateTime, toOffsetDateTime and toOffsetTime can still throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) and tests are all required. error_model is required because the change adds a new error path whose message ends up saying 'Bad value for type timestamp/date/time: ' with nothing after it.

build_ci is required because this PR changes the pinned version of a CI dependency (actions/checkout v6.0.3 to v6.1.0) in 14 workflow files, including release and token-using steps. A reviewer should check that the SHA matches the v6.1.0 tag and that the minor bump changes nothing about how CI behaves.
No axis is labeled 2. This PR only adds a regression test for COLUMN_DEF in getColumns: a quick look at the test's assertions and the empty description is enough.

This PR hardens how the driver parses untrusted wire-protocol input: it adds frame-length caps, bounds on read-buffer growth, and fixes to C-string scanning and GSS parsing. So security, correctness, spec_conformance, performance, tests and error_model all need a focused check, and backward_compat and surprising_behavior do too because the new hard caps (32 MiB buffer, 10000-byte small messages) and the broken-connection or truncation behavior can affect existing users. Contradictions, doc_comments and change_description are required because some descriptions don't match the code: the MAX_SMALL_MESSAGE_LENGTH comment cites libpq's 30000 but sets 10000, the description says oversized ErrorResponse/NoticeResponse bodies are skipped and truncated while the visible code rejects them up front, and the changelog files fixes under 'Changed'.

build_ci is required: the PR updates the Gradle wrapper and its checksum, and moves the Android Gradle Plugin up a major version (8.13 to 9.3), which can break the Android sample and test modules and change the minimum JDK or Gradle versions the build needs.

correctness is required because the PR changes how captured wildcards and their backing wildcard bounds are handled. It also changes how RHS wildcards are compared in CheckIdenticalNullabilityVisitor, and both involve edge cases (UNBOUND, SUPER, when the flag is disabled). spec_conformance is required because this changes how NullAway reads JSpecify wildcard and capture nullability semantics.

Correctness needs a focused check because the PR adds non-trivial cycle detection and copies javac TypeVar/CapturedType objects with overridden baseType() and a reassigned tsym, which may not hold up across JDK versions. Tests are owed because the changed visitor paths (unbounded wildcards, F-bounded cycles) are only tested at checker level in #1668, and spec_conformance is owed because the code applies JSpecify's rule on the implicit upper bounds of unbounded wildcards.

change_description is labeled 2 because this bug fix changes what users see in JSpecify mode (fewer false positives for types like BiConsumer), so it needs a changelog entry, and the PR doesn't include one. Tests and correctness are only a glance: the BiConsumer regression test fails without the fix, and the change from Map to SetMultimap is small and the same everywhere it's used.

Tests, correctness and spec_conformance are required: the change alters how JSpecify generic inference works for anonymous diamond classes, and the new fallback returns NULLABLE for any anonymous enclosing symbol whose type is null, which could hide real errors in cases the PR never meant to cover. A focused reviewer should check that fallback, the direct-supertype matching logic, and whether the tests exercise those edge cases.

The description says the check reads only the org.jspecify annotations and ships at SUGGESTION, but the Javadoc and @BugPattern say it matches annotations by simple name (plus NullAway's custom-annotation flags) at WARNING, and the CheckLocalVariableRootType flag it describes isn't visible in the code shown. That puts contradictions, change_description, doc_comments, user_docs, backward_compat and surprising_behavior at 2, since users could see new warnings on upgrade. This is a large new check that implements the JSpecify spec, so spec_conformance, correctness, tests and user_value are required by policy.

Correctness is required because the PR changes how raw array types and unbound method-reference qualifiers get their types, and that is tricky logic. Change_description and contradictions are required because the description only talks about raw arrays and #1800, while the code also adds a method-reference resolver with tests for issue #1795 that the description never mentions.

tests is required: the PR changes how nullability is inferred for takeWhile on Java Stream, RxJava Observable and Reactor Flux, but adds no tests. There should be at least one positive and one negative test for each of the three stream libraries.

build_ci is required because the PR changes the GitHub Actions workflow triggers (merge_group) and the concurrency group expression. The expression looks right: PRs are grouped by number, and master pushes and merge-queue runs get a unique run_id, so they are never cancelled.

build_ci and security are required because this adds a CI workflow and dependency-update automation, and the unpinned renovate:latest image plus the supply-chain cooldown are security concerns. contradictions and correctness are required because the description promises a 7-day minimumReleaseAge with exemptions and custom regex managers, neither of which appears in renovate.json, and the JSONata alias rules and Gradle ranges need checking.

Correctness is required because the PR changes complex logic for restoring nullness through wildcard capture: super and lower-bounded wildcards now fall through, and wildcard and type-variable copies are made instead of changing javac's shared bounds. Tests are required because this is a bug fix, and the change in GenericsUtils that lets an explicit annotation on the formal upper bound override library-model or unmarked-code nullability has no dedicated test.

correctness and tests are required because this bug fix rewrites the logic for wildcard/capture upper bounds and nullness inference, which is non-trivial and needs regression coverage that can actually fail. spec_conformance is required because the change reinterprets JLS capture conversion and wildcard containment under JSpecify nullness rules.
